data.summary: This guide explains the age policy for kids and teens on yacht charters in Marbella, covering minimum ages, safety requirements, and recommended boats for families departing Puerto Banús.
key_facts: Minimum age for infants is 12 months on most charters.
Children under 12 must wear a life jacket at all times on deck.
Teens aged 12+ can use jet skis with adult supervision (Tier B boats).
Family-friendly boats include Astondoa 40 (9 pax) and Lagoon 380 (10 pax).
All charters include licensed skipper and safety equipment.
Puerto Banús departures offer calm waters ideal for young children.

faq.q: What is the minimum age for kids on a Marbella yacht charter?
faq.a: Most charters accept infants from 12 months old. For safety, children under 12 must wear a life jacket on deck. Always confirm with the operator when booking, as some boats may have different policies for very young children.

faq.q: Can teenagers drive a jet ski during the charter?
faq.a: Yes, teenagers aged 12 and over can drive a jet ski on Tier B boats like the Mangusta 80, but only under direct adult supervision. The jet ski is included free for 4-hour+ charters on these boats.

faq.q: Are life jackets provided for children?
faq.a: Yes, life jackets in various sizes are provided free of charge for all children. We recommend bringing a favourite floatie or swim vest for added comfort, but our safety equipment covers all ages.

faq.q: Which boats are best for families with young kids?
faq.a: Boats with spacious decks and stable hulls are ideal. The Lagoon 380 (catamaran, 10 pax) offers excellent stability and shade. The Astondoa 40 (9 pax) has a large cockpit area, perfect for toddlers.

faq.q: Is there a minimum age for booking a private charter?
faq.a: No, there is no minimum age for the charter itself. All ages are welcome, but the responsible adult must be at least 18 years old to sign the contract. Children are counted in the total passenger capacity.

faq.q: What safety measures are in place for kids on board?
faq.a: All charters include a licensed skipper trained in safety protocols, plus life jackets, first aid kits, and safety briefing before departure. The skipper will advise on safe areas for swimming and playing.

faq.q: Can we bring baby food or special snacks?
faq.a: Absolutely. You are welcome to bring your own baby food, snacks, and drinks. Our standard inclusions cover water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, and light snacks, but special dietary needs are your responsibility.

faq.q: Are there any age restrictions for swimming stops?
faq.a: No age restrictions for swimming, but children under 12 must wear a life jacket in the water unless a parent is holding them. Our skippers choose calm spots like Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés, ideal for families.

data.body_html:
Planning a family yacht charter in Marbella? Understanding the marbella yacht charter age policy for kids and teens ensures a safe and enjoyable day on the water. From minimum ages to safety gear and recommended boats, here’s everything you need to know before setting sail from Puerto Banús.

Minimum Age Requirements for Children

Most charters accept infants from 12 months old. For safety, children under 12 must wear a life jacket whenever on deck. Always confirm your child’s age when booking, as some boats may have stricter policies. The skipper will provide a safety briefing for the whole family.

Life Jackets and Safety Gear

Life jackets in child and toddler sizes are supplied free on every charter. Our fleet includes boats like the Astondoa 40 and Lagoon 380, both with ample deck space for kids to move safely. The skipper will also demonstrate emergency procedures and point out safety equipment locations.

Teens and Jet Ski Use

Teens aged 12 and over can drive a jet ski on Tier B boats (e.g., Mangusta 80) but only with adult supervision. The jet ski is included free on 4-hour+ charters. For younger teens, consider a slower speedboat like the Speedboat (7m, 6 pax) for a more controlled experience.

Best Boats for Families with Kids

Choose stable, spacious boats for young children. The Lagoon 380 (catamaran, 10 pax) offers minimal rocking and shaded areas. The Astondoa 40 (9 pax) has a large aft deck, perfect for toddlers. For larger families, the Azimut 58 Flybridge (12 pax) provides plenty of room and a flybridge for teens to enjoy the view.

Swimming and Water Activities

All ages are welcome to swim at stops like Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés. Children under 12 must wear a life jacket in the water unless held by an adult. The skipper will choose calm, shallow spots ideal for family dips. Bring your own snorkel gear for the kids — our charter packages include soft drinks and snacks to keep everyone energised.

Booking and Passenger Limits

Children count towards the total passenger capacity. For example, the Astondoa 40 holds 9 pax total, so a family of 4 adults and 5 kids fits perfectly. The Azimut 39 (11 pax) offers more flexibility. Always mention children’s ages when booking to ensure the right boat and safety equipment.

What’s Included for Families

Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, life jackets, and a safety briefing. Drinks (water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava) and light snacks are provided. You can bring your own baby food or special snacks — no problem. The skipper will also help with any specific needs, like finding a quiet spot for nap time.

Most charters accept infants from 12 months old. For safety, children under 12 must wear a life jacket on deck. Always confirm with the operator when booking, as some boats may have different policies for very young children.

Yes, teenagers aged 12 and over can drive a jet ski on Tier B boats like the Mangusta 80, but only under direct adult supervision. The jet ski is included free for 4-hour+ charters on these boats.

Yes, life jackets in various sizes are provided free of charge for all children. We recommend bringing a favourite floatie or swim vest for added comfort, but our safety equipment covers all ages.

Boats with spacious decks and stable hulls are ideal. The Lagoon 380 (catamaran, 10 pax) offers excellent stability and shade. The Astondoa 40 (9 pax) has a large cockpit area, perfect for toddlers.

Is there a minimum age for booking a private charter?

No, there is no minimum age for the charter itself. All ages are welcome, but the responsible adult must be at least 18 years old to sign the contract. Children are counted in the total passenger capacity.

What safety measures are in place for kids on board?

All charters include a licensed skipper trained in safety protocols, plus life jackets, first aid kits, and safety briefing before departure. The skipper will advise on safe areas for swimming and playing.

No age restrictions for swimming, but children under 12 must wear a life jacket in the water unless a parent is holding them. Our skippers choose calm spots like Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés, ideal for families.
